entries.detail: HTTP 403 via both WebFetch and direct curl, and no Wayback snapshot exists, so only a web-search snippet of the record was seen (existence and title). The May 2004 date, evaluation criteria and purpose were corroborated through the Borth Community website (R4) instead; the authors of the May 2004 study are still unknown (card gap).

entries.what: As-built plan, post-construction survey or reef-only rock quantity for the Borth reef (Phase 1, completed 8 March 2012)
entries.where: web searches 2026-10-06/07; Ceredigion County Council monitoring reports; Wales Coastal Monitoring Centre (wcmc.wales) map; CoastSnap Borth
entries.detail: Not found at a primary source: an as-built plan, a post-construction survey of the reef, or a reef-only rock volume or tonnage (the 3D model uses the Royal Haskoning design drawings 9V5090/1020-1023 and the 2022 Welsh Government LiDAR instead). Ceredigion's annual beach monitoring (Royal HaskoningDHV Vol I 2012-13) has LiDAR-derived beach profiles only, no reef levels. The Wales Coastal Monitoring Centre is an interactive map with no readable static values, and CoastSnap Borth photos (2024-25) exist but were not checked for the reef. The design bed level (about -4.0 mODN) therefore limits the model.
entries.might_work: Lior: Phase 1 as-built drawings from Ceredigion County Council or the contractor (BAM Nuttall); a post-2022 drone or boat sounding

entries.what: Highest astronomical tide (HAT), Z0 and chart-datum offsets for Aberystwyth
entries.where: NTSLF 'Chart datum and ordnance datum' table; UKHO-derived harbour pages; tide-forecast.com listing; searches 2026-10-06
entries.detail: HAT not found at a primary source (the NTSLF table lists Barmouth and Fishguard, -2.44 m, but not Aberystwyth; the only HAT-like figure, 5.9 m CD, is a predicted maximum). Secondary harbour pages give MHWS 5.0 / MHWN 3.5 / MLWN 1.8 / MLWS 0.7 m CD, consistent with LAT -2.44 mODN. MSL (+0.31 mODN) is a four-level mean with +-0.15 m. So the tide slider stops at MHWS.
entries.might_work: Lior: W3 / REQUESTS row 6 (UKHO EasyTide or Admiralty Tide Tables Vol 1, Aberystwyth)

entries.what: Garmin / Navionics web viewer at Borth for the reef or a depth at it
entries.by: agent: Borth 3D agent (cloud, own headless Chrome)
entries.detail: No login or CAPTCHA appeared. The chart shows no reef symbol, no obstruction and no depth at the rock; its datum is not stated (LAT assumed, best of 7 by RMS) and its offshore contours are 0.6-1.1 m shallower than the pre-construction survey (Fig 2) and EMODnet, so it was not used for the model. The Navionics app may show an obstruction symbol that the web viewer does not.
entries.might_work: Lior: Navionics app rows 1-3 in the Borth 3D REQUESTS_FOR_LIOR.md

entries.what: EMODnet DTM 2024 cells at Borth and CDI survey record 115084 (survey date and datum)
entries.detail: The reef cells (-0.34 to -0.13 m LAT) are GEBCO fill (interpolated), not survey values; the real source cells (CDI 115084) have one sounding per cell, age over 30 years and unknown horizontal accuracy, and start 335 m from the defence line. The CDI page sits behind a bot check / block page (not bypassed), so the survey date and datum were not read. Only the LAT statement and a seaward gradient of about -1.1 % are used. No finer data (nearest high-resolution DTM, CHERISH Wales, is 22 km north).
entries.might_work: Lior: W2 (open CDI 115084 in a normal browser and the EMODnet viewer 'Source Reference of the DTM')

entries.what: Esri Wayback frames of Borth 2017-05-09 and 2020-03-26, and the current z18/z17 frames
entries.detail: 2017-05-09: cloud cover; 2020-03-26: low contrast, reef partly submerged and in spray; the z18/z17 current frames covered the wrong area (cliffs 1.7 km south) or only context. Deleted and not used. The traced outline comes from 2024-09-17 and 2022-08-25 (low tide, rock bare); 2012-10-27 and 2013-06-04 are used as cross-checks.
entries.might_work: Lior: lowest-water Google Earth Pro image (G7)

entries.what: Gemini's Borth sources and footprint (200 x 200 m, 12,500 m2, 110,000 t, Halcrow; 'Ceredigion Final Review 2013', 'BAM Nuttall case study 2012', 'Coflein Craig y Delyn Reef 2015')
entries.detail: The Ceredigion 'Final Review 2013' and the BAM Nuttall 'case study 2012' do not exist as far as searched; the Coflein record is actually 'Coastal Defences, Borth' (NPRN 424699, record 2020), not 'Craig y Delyn Reef 2015'. The 200 x 200 m footprint does not match the drawings, LiDAR or imagery, and 200 m offshore is contradicted by two live sources (300-400 m). Gemini lead not confirmed; nothing used.

entries.what: Borth image leads: geograph 2554717 (construction fence) and Wikimedia 'A bigger splash' barge photo
entries.detail: The geograph photo shows a chain-link fence and 'Construction Operations KEEP OUT' sign with the beach behind and no reef visible offshore; the Wikimedia photo shows a barge delivering rock armour (the works, not the reef in place). Site context only. A video frame (QUB6s_F9dZc_0007) shows onshore stockpiling of rock, not the offshore reef.

entries.what: YouTube videos QUB6s_F9dZc 'Borth Beach Sea Defence Works August 2011' and dQieZVQUDEI 'borth sea defence 2012' as footage of the reef
entries.result: other: video shows the works, not the reef
entries.detail: Silent amateur construction b-roll. The saved frame QUB6s_F9dZc_0007 shows houses, plant and a stockpile of quarried rock on the seafront (onshore works, not the offshore reef); dQieZVQUDEI is a Komatsu 450 separating rock and shingle (material preparation), judged on its description only (embed not possible, no download). The other two Borth videos (c4J6hfvynr4, AJXnUqQObJM) do show the reef under construction.
